summary: The student has successfully created a functional Windows Forms Name Display Application that meets all core requirements. The application features a button that when clicked displays a name in a label, with proper event handling and form initialization. The code follows good naming conventions using descriptive names (ShowNameButton, NameLabel) instead of abbreviated prefixes, and includes appropriate comments explaining the key logic.

requirementResults.requirement: Button triggers name display in a label
requirementResults.feedback: The ShowNameButton_Click event handler correctly assigns the author's name to the NameLabel.Text property when the button is clicked.

requirementResults.requirement: Follow C# naming conventions (prefer CamelCase, avoid abbreviations)
requirementResults.feedback: Excellent naming conventions used: ShowNameButton and NameLabel follow proper CamelCase for controls and are descriptive without abbreviations.
Good commenting throughout. Comments explain the component initialization, variable creation, and the purpose of setting the label's Text property.

issues.message: Form title is set to 'Form1' instead of something more descriptive like 'Name Display App'
issues.suggestion: Consider changing the Form Text property to something more descriptive for better user experience

positives: Excellent use of descriptive control names (ShowNameButton, NameLabel) instead of default or abbreviated names
Proper event handler implementation with correct signature and functionality
Clean, well-organized code structure with appropriate separation of form logic and designer code
Good commenting practice explaining key operations
Correct use of camelCase for local variables (authorName)
Proper Windows Forms application structure with Program.cs entry point
Successful implementation of all core assignment requirements
